newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso recovers at close from C Bank move.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso recovers at close from C Bank move.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank's strong defense of the peso helped it recover at the close after it was battered by fears of large outflows from the stock market, traders said.

The Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate by 0.75 percentage-point to 11 percent to make it more expensive for banks to hold on to dollars. It also flooded banks with dollars worth $123 to $129 million at 26.37/26.375.
The peso ended at 26.37 after being pounded to a day-low of 26.375 in midsession.
"The smoke cleared when the Central Bank offered the overnight rate at 11 percent," a trader said.
"This is a preemptive move. This is just to calm the market," Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters.
The Central Bank's action immediately lifted the peso to its day-high of 26.368 but it was pulled down again by banks who preferred to buy dollars, traders said.
"At the end of the day it was more of position squaring. Those who bought more than they need sold," another dealer said.
The peso's direction would depend on how the local stock market will fare, traders said.
The equities market had tumbled to a two-year low due to dismal first quarter earnings and fears of a slump in the property segment.
The Central Bank said it saw no capital flight from foreign funds divesting from the stock market.
The peso averaged at 26.373 for the day compared with the previous 26.369. Market volume more than doubled to $324 million from $150.9 million.
